name: Media Alternative (Prerecorded)
explanation: This criterion applies to prerecorded video that has a synchronized audio track — a training video, a webinar recording, a product demo with narration. It requires a full text alternative: a single document that both describes everything happening visually and transcribes everything said or heard, in the correct order, well enough that someone could understand the entire video by reading it alone. This goes further than captions, which only transcribe the audio, and further than audio description, which narrates visuals into the soundtrack but still requires watching or listening in real time. A media alternative must be offered regardless of whether audio description is already provided, specifically so that someone who cannot use audio or video at all, not just someone who can't see or can't hear, has a way to get the same content.
whoItAffects: Deaf-blind users who read a braille display can't perceive video or audio at all, so a full text alternative is often the only way they can access the content. Captions and audio description both depend on being able to perceive at least one media track, so they don't help this group. People with unreliable or very limited bandwidth, or in a context where playing audio or video isn't possible, can read the transcript-plus-description instead of streaming the video. Some users with cognitive or learning disabilities also prefer or need to read content at their own pace, re-reading sections, rather than following a fixed-speed video and audio track.

codeExample.bad:
<!-- Training video has captions and an audio description track, but there is no way
     to get the content without playing the video — nothing works for someone who can't
     perceive audio or video at all, such as a deaf-blind user on a braille display. -->
<video controls width="640" height="360">
  <source src="onboarding-training.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <track kind="captions" src="onboarding-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">
  <track kind="descriptions" src="onboarding-ad-en.vtt" srclang="en" label="English audio description">
  Your browser does not support the video tag.
</video>
codeExample.good: Read the full text alternative, which describes every on-screen action and transcribes all narration and dialogue.

howToTest: Find the link to the text alternative near the video. It's often labeled 'text alternative' or 'full transcript' — don't confuse it with a captions file or a bare dialogue-only transcript. Open it without playing the video, and read it start to finish. Check two things: does it describe every visually important moment, and does it also capture everything said or heard? It passes if you can understand the full content of the video from that document alone, including the parts that were only ever shown, never spoken. It fails if the document only has dialogue with no description of visuals, or doesn't exist at all.

check.question: A prerecorded webinar recording already has captions and an audio description track. According to SC 1.2.8, is a full text alternative still required?
choices: No — captions plus audio description together already satisfy every text alternative requirement at any level
Yes — a full text alternative describing all visuals and transcribing all audio must still be offered, so someone who cannot perceive audio or video at all can access the content
No — a text alternative is only needed if the webinar has no captions
Yes, but only the spoken dialogue needs to be included; on-screen visuals can be left out since audio description already covers them
